name: VampHunt cross-artifact rules
policy: Every match is a lead and must retain the normalized source events that caused it.

rules.title: Executable or script referenced from a user-writable directory
rules.description: Execution-oriented artifacts reference a program or script under Downloads, Temp, AppData, ProgramData, or Users\Public.

rules.title: Credential-access or reconnaissance utility observed
rules.description: An artifact references a utility commonly used to recover credentials, dump process memory, or enumerate Active Directory.

rules.title: Remote execution utility observed
rules.description: An artifact references a utility that can execute commands on another Windows system.

rules.title: Windows system binary name outside an expected directory
rules.description: An execution-oriented artifact uses a Windows system binary name from a path outside Windows system and component-store directories.

rules.title: Deceptive double-extension executable
rules.description: A file name combines a document or image extension with an executable or script extension.

rules.title: Program execution followed by deletion
rules.description: The same executable or script is present in execution evidence and the Recycle Bin within thirty days.

rules.title: User-writable program corroborated by multiple artifacts
rules.description: A program in a user-writable directory is referenced by at least two independent forensic artifact types.

rules.title: Suspicious command configured to run at user logon
rules.description: A Run or RunOnce value invokes a script interpreter, uses high-risk command options, or pairs a misleading value name with a program in a user-writable directory.

rules.title: Debugger or monitor configured for program launch
rules.description: Image File Execution Options or SilentProcessExit names another program to run when a target starts or exits. This can redirect execution for persistence or defense evasion.

rules.title: AppInit DLL configured
rules.description: The AppInit_DLLs value contains a DLL path, which can load code into processes that use User32.dll.

rules.title: Windows logon program changed from its default
rules.description: A Winlogon Shell or Userinit value points somewhere other than the normal Windows program.

rules.title: Service program stored in a user-writable directory
rules.description: A service ImagePath points to an executable or script under a directory ordinary users or applications commonly write to.

rules.title: Microsoft Defender exclusion found
rules.description: A Defender exclusion removes a path, process, extension, or address from normal inspection. Confirm that the setting was approved.

rules.title: High-risk command preserved in Run history
rules.description: Explorer Run history contains an encoded, hidden, downloaded, or directly evaluated command.

rules.title: Shortcut contains high-risk command options
rules.description: A Windows shortcut contains command options commonly used to hide, encode, download, or directly evaluate code.

rules.title: Shortcut launches a program from a network share
rules.description: A Windows shortcut launches an executable or script from a UNC path or recorded network share.

rules.title: Executable or script has a named NTFS data stream
rules.description: An executable or script has a named data stream other than the normal Zone.Identifier download marker. Review the stream contents and origin.

rules.title: Executable has inconsistent NTFS creation times
rules.description: The Standard Information creation time of an executable or script substantially predates its File Name creation time. Copying can cause this, so review it as possible timestamp manipulation rather than proof.

rules.title: Executable or script created and quickly deleted
rules.description: USN records show the same executable or script being created and deleted within thirty minutes, and an independent execution artifact corroborates the program from a risky location or known dual-use name.

rules.title: Many documents renamed to the same new extension
rules.description: USN rename pairs show many documents receiving the same unfamiliar extension in a five-minute window, a pattern associated with bulk file encryption.

rules.title: Windows event log deleted
rules.description: USN records show deletion of a Windows event-log file. Confirm whether log retention or maintenance explains it.

rules.title: Windows Registry hive deleted
rules.description: USN records show deletion of a Windows Registry hive. This can be normal during profile removal, so correlate it with account and system activity.

rules.title: New account added to a privileged group
rules.description: Security events connect a newly created account to membership in a privileged local or domain group within one hour.

rules.title: Repeated failed logons followed by a success
rules.description: Five or more failed Security logons from the same address to the same account are followed by a successful logon within fifteen minutes.

rules.title: Risky service program corroborated by execution evidence
rules.description: A service-install event points to a user-writable or known dual-use program also present in Prefetch, Amcache, Shimcache, shortcut, or jump-list evidence.

rules.title: Scheduled task references a risky observed program
rules.description: A task-creation event references a user-writable or known dual-use program corroborated by execution-oriented artifacts.

rules.title: Suspicious PowerShell content linked to an observed program
rules.description: A PowerShell script-block event contains high-risk behavior and names a program also present in execution-oriented evidence.

rules.title: Defender protection disabled before risky execution
rules.description: A Microsoft Defender protection-disabled event is followed by a user-writable or known dual-use program observed in execution evidence within two hours.

rules.title: Risky observed program used the network
rules.description: SRUM attributes sent or received bytes to a user-writable or known dual-use program that is independently present in execution-oriented artifacts.
